title: Region fleet handoff and contingency notes — 2026-04-08
content:
Summary:

Weekly infrastructure update focusing on regional fleet handoff, contingency playbook refresh, and short-term capacity hedging for the next 3 weeks. This doc captures the operational signal we saw last weekend, decisions made in the 2026-04-08 on-call huddle, and concrete actions for regional owners ahead of the upcoming marketing release window (customer pilot X launching 2026-04-15).

Attendees:
- Marco Ruiz (owner)
- Aisha Patel (fleet ops)
- Dana Chen (SRE)
- Liam O'Connor (platform eng)
- Priya Narang (capacity planning)
- On-call rotation: eng-infra-weekend-1

Key observations (last 7 days):
- Increased tail latency from eu-west1 during short A/B test spikes (median p95 jump from 210ms to 480ms between 2026-04-03 22:30 UTC and 2026-04-04 01:10 UTC).
- APAC (ap-south1) warm pool underutilized but slow to scale due to image pull bottleneck on some H100 nodes.
- US-WEST A100 pool reached 78% sustained utilization during internal load test; no SLAs breached but margin reduced for handling bursty requests.
- Prewarming experiment v2 (decreasing cold-start count by proactively initializing model instances with cached KV shards) reduced cold-start tail latency by ~28% in eu-west1 in test runs (see linked PR).

Immediate risks and triggers:
- Risk: marketing release (pilot X) scheduled for 2026-04-15 may increase token throughput by up to 2.1x on eu-west1 during hours 14:00-20:00 UTC. Trigger: sustained 60-minute rolling increase >1.6x above baseline.
- Risk: H100 image-pull failures causing 10–12 minute provisioning delays in ap-south1. Trigger: >3 failures in 1 hour for distinct nodes.
- Risk: billing cap exhaustion for reserved Dedicated pools in US-WEST if utilization stays >75% for 4 consecutive days. Trigger: forecasted burn rate crossing committed threshold (Priya to monitor).

Decisions made (huddle 2026-04-08):
- Prepositioning: Move +16 L4 instances from us-east to eu-west1 on 2026-04-12 02:00 UTC as a short-term hedging step (non-disruptive live migration using cold-alloc semantics). Responsible: Liam O'Connor.
- Burst capacity reservations: Open temporary burst reservation for us-west A100 pool for the weekend of 2026-04-11 to 2026-04-13 (4 hours/day peak window). Responsible: Priya Narang to coordinate procurement with cloud ops.
- Canary prewarming rollout: Expand prewarming v2 to 20% of eu-west1 traffic starting 2026-04-09; monitor cold-starts, tail latency, and memory overhead. Responsible: Aisha Patel (runbook in linked PR).
- Contingency fallback policy: If eu-west1 p95 > 450ms for >30m, route 30% of traffic to regional fallback models (smaller quantized variants) in us-west until metric stabilizes. Responsible: Marco Ruiz to update smart routing policy.

Action items (owner — due):
- Aisha Patel — finalize prewarming rollout checklist and update runbook with KVM cache size thresholds (due 2026-04-09).
- Priya Narang — finalize burst reservation order and payment; escalate to finance if procurement delay >24h (due 2026-04-10).
- Liam O'Connor — schedule and validate non-disruptive L4 migration test in staging, include image-pull remediation patch in rolling agent update (due 2026-04-11).
- Dana Chen — add an automated alert to paging for image-pull error rate in ap-south1 and attach remediation playbook (JIRA-INFRA-1499) (due 2026-04-09).
- Marco Ruiz — update smart-routing policies to include temporary fallback percentage and notify product partners (due 2026-04-10).

Operational run notes and checks performed:
- Healthcheck sweep completed 2026-04-07 23:00 UTC: identified 12 instances with kernel OOM logs across eu-west1 candidates; those nodes were cordoned and reprovisioned; logs forwarded to eng-sre for deeper analysis.
- Capacity forecast snapshot (Priya): baseline daily tokens = 1.2B, expected pilot uplift = +1.0B tokens/day (peak scenarios). Current reserved headroom across regions = 0.9B tokens/day. Shortfall window = 6 days if pilot sustained at peak.
- Experiment results: prewarming v2 memory overhead measured at +4% per instance, cold-start tail latency reduction consistent at 25–32% across runs. Decision: accept overhead for canary.

Communication plan:
- Notify product and solutions engineering this afternoon with a summary and expected temporary routing changes.
- Slack channel #infra-ops: short status posts on 2026-04-09 and 2026-04-11 highlighting canary metrics and any scaling actions.
- Escalation: If any trigger fires, SRE lead will open an incident channel and brief CS for customer-facing communications.

Follow-ups and long-term items (for roadmap):
- Investigate region-level image distribution optimizations to reduce H100 provisioning delays (storage caching tier / pre-pulled images).
- Revisit committed capacity sizing model to include probabilistic burst hedging (Priya and finance).
- Explore automated dynamic fallback percentages tied to cold-start metrics rather than fixed percentages.

Notes to self / quick reminders (informal):
- Keep the canary window tight; instrument extra traces on kv-cache miss rates.
- Check with security about any changes to KMS rotation when migrating L4 instances cross-region.
- Follow up with customer success on pilot X expected traffic shape (ask for synthetic load profile).

Appendix / references:
- Prewarming PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-config/pull/328
- Capacity hedging playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INFRA-HEDGING-STRAT
- Incident ticket for ap-south1 image pulls: JIRA-INFRA-1499

End of notes.
